summary: Cross-subaccount quota misattribution during canary routing rollout causing unexpected 429s
description: Customer BrightDocs reported intermittent 429s starting 2026-03-10 09:14 UTC. Issue appeared coincident with a staged canary rollout of a new routing policy that adds per-route weighting for low-latency traffic. Initial analysis shows tokens billed to the wrong subaccount (child accounts A vs B), causing one subaccount's quota to deplete and trigger tenant-level throttle behavior. This ticket tracks investigation and remediation for the production incident affecting BrightDocs' enterprise account.
impact: ~18% of BrightDocs' requests for low-latency route returned 429s over a 42-minute window. Customer reports degraded user-facing search autocomplete and failing background reranks; business impact: degraded SLA and two-minute outages for a small fraction of users.
timeline:
2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - Canary rollout started (routing-service v2.7.1).
2026-03-10 09:14 UTC - BrightDocs reports first 429s.
2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - Support engaged SRE.
2026-03-10 09:56 UTC - Canary roll back hinted; additional logs captured.
2026-03-11 03:10 UTC - Hotfix PR opened to correct accounting logic.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Set up two subaccounts (child-A, child-B) under same tenant with separate per-route weights.
2) Deploy routing-service v2.7.1 with canary enabled for 10% of traffic routing to low-latency pool.
3) Execute mixed workload: frequent short streams (~200ms tokens) + periodic batch rerank jobs.
4) Observe rate-limit headers and per-subaccount usage in console; compare billed token attribution.
Note: Repro is non-deterministic and requires multiplexed short-lived sessions to trigger misattribution path.

support_comments:
Customer: 'We started seeing 429s around 09:14 UTC during normal traffic; nothing changed on our side.'
Support (Marina): Captured request IDs and console screenshots; escalated to SRE and requested a timeline.
SRE (Jared): 'Reproducing locally with canary weight and short sessions shows accounting drift; collecting metrics.'
investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis: routing canary path bypasses per-subaccount attribution in the rate-limiter when requests are proxied through new host selection layer.
- Metrics show spikes in token accounting attributed to subA while requests originated from subB sessions.
- Correlated with changes in x-forwarded-subaccount handling in routing-service v2.7.1 (PR 889).
- Audit of rate-limiter code revealed an edge case: when canary=true and host affinity is used, the subaccount id header is overwritten by internal host-metadata, leading to misattribution.
- Confirmed by reproducer harness: toggling canary flag flips attribution to the host's default subaccount id.
mitigation_steps:
1) Immediate: disable canary rollouts to low-latency route for all customers (rolled back 2026-03-10 10:04 UTC).
2) Short-term workaround: enable strict header validation at api-gateway to reject requests where subaccount header is missing or altered.
3) Customer advised: staggered retry with exponential backoff; increased per-route burst credit temporarily requested and granted for BrightDocs.
resolution_summary: Patch merged to rate-limiter to preserve original subaccount attribution when canary routing is active (PR github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/commit/abc1234). Canary rollout paused until canary path validated end-to-end. BrightDocs quota reconciled: misattributed tokens moved back to correct subaccount in billing ledger (manual reconciliation completed 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC).
follow_up_tasks: Add unit/integration tests for canary path header preservation
Add metrics/alert for token-attribution-anomalies per subaccount
Run full billing reconciliation audit for affected time window
Hardening: API-gateway enforce canonical subaccount header and log mismatches
customer_response: BrightDocs: 'Thanks for the quick rollback and reconciliation. We'd like a follow-up call to review safeguards before you resume the route canary.'
owner_notes: Assigning to routing-service and rate-limiter owners for coordinated rollback and QA. Target: ship v2.7.2 with accounting tests before next canary. Jared to coordinate QA with SEs and BrightDocs for a validation window.
public_status_note: Internal: issue caused by canary routing path; customer quota impact fixed and tokens reconciled. Ops: canary paused while we validate fix. Status page event created for investigative window.
